title: Tagging rules: New tagging column/feature
description:
Adds a new "Tagging Rules" concept separate from Coloring Rules. Tagging Rules let users associate a visual tag (emoji, text, or both) with packets that match a display filter expression, displayed in a dedicated Tag (tagging rules) column. Allows the tag to store a URL to be able to click through to associate documentation, or anything else with the packet that matches the rule.

AI Assisted: yes

notes.body:
`COL_EMOJI` is a very generic name for this coloring rules specific feature. Can this new feature be made more generic?

Example: As a user I would like to show all packets having an expert_info (display filter `_ws.expert`) with a specific emoji without having the same coloring rule for all packets having expert_info. The same for other display filters which may or may not be the same as a coloring rule.

I think this could be a separate feature, similar to the coloring rules but only for the new "emoji" column.

Interesting... I initially had this as part of the paint of the color for the row without the dedicate column. I had showed this to Roland, and he had given me the feedback to make this a new TYPE column. But I see the use case, and thinking through it how I have been using it for the last couple weeks. I could have/want row color, and emoji in the same rule. I have also the case where I have just the row color in no emoji. But here to have emoji and no color on the row. if I split this into a new feature having a filter match for emoji, and a filter match for color. I could be doubling the work if I want emoji and color on the same filter.

the compatibility I concentrated on was multi-color rule matching, so it would would show multiple emoji's if more that one rule matches. Since users are used to going to "coloring rules" to enter a filter and highlighting a certain packet (up til now only a color). Instead of a different place to do emoji's, what if I had a check box that allows the user to not have foreground/background, thus only having the emoji display. Right now if the emoji box is empty it just does foreground/background. this would kind of do the same thing in reverse. and with the multi-color ability it could match the more specific rules, and more broad rules on same packet. Thoughts?

as I wrote this, there might be a want to just display the top match color, but display all matching emoji's.

thoughts on something like this?
![image](/uploads/5face6d9f97c342ff72d6c20d60b03d3/image.png){width=900 height=557}

I still think this is a different feature and does not belong in the coloring rules.

I think it will be hard to understand when this is mixed in the coloring rules.
* The coloring rules stop at first match, the "emoji" column uses all.
* The coloring rules works on each row, the "emoji" is a column with multiple values.
* Users would like to configure them independently.
* Having an "Emoji" in a coloring rule does not really make sense in my head.

Remember you can always configure an "emoji" using a filter to match a specific coloring rule.

just to address some of your highlights. I did this as a expansion on the multi-color rule match display. with the inspiration being I had multiple rules match that were red (or various shades of red), and wanted a way to visually show different rules really matched. I initially had this as part of the row paint, but it did have the possibility of display the emoji over text in a column. When I showed this at sharkfest, that's when was brought up to add it as a column.

* The coloring rules stop at first match, the "emoji" column uses all.
   ![image](/uploads/7ce47acae7bd25ed5a7dffd49c416542/image.png){width=900 height=223}
 example of multiple coloring rules match with each having an emoji.
* The coloring rules works on each row, the "emoji" is a column with multiple values.
   agreed, not as ituitive as just making a coloring rule, and clicking ok. Though I would have no   objection to making it part of the row paint instead of the column.

* Users would like to configure them independently.
   agreed. I just didn't want to have to fill in two different spots if I wanted a row colored and a emoji. I'd like to go to one spot, put in a filter and say it's a row color(background/foreground), or emoji, or both.

* Having an "Emoji" in a coloring rule does not really make sense in my head.
  the way it made sense for me was this is the natural place I would go to highlight a packet. Whether that highlight of the packet is a color, or an emoji, or something else.

Is this new column restricted to emoji's only or can it also contain text?

What happens in version 4.6.x when loading a `colorfilters` created with the new emoji? It must be backward compatible somehow.

Right now it can contain text.

With emoji the config line is @Name@filter@[r,g,b][r,g,b]@🔥\n

I just put the emoji as the 5th  field appended to the existing line.

in 4.6.x fscanf parses the two [r,g,b] color groups,  then sets skip_end_of_line = true, and the skip loop at the top of the next iteration reads every byte until \n while reading @🔥 silently.

Maybe "emoji" is the wrong name for this column? I think it looks more like a filter flag, or a filter marker, or something like that. At least if it's possible to configure anything to be shown in this column, not only emojis.

I didn't check for compatibility, but very good you checked that it will not cause issues.

I'm not married to any particular name for the column. But to be honest, the ability for text to show is just a happy accident, or biproduct of what I was trying to accomplish. I didn't have a usecase to show "text", I could put some checks in there to try and lock this down and not allow just text.

This feature very much resembles a feature I once started to develop, but stopped. I wanted a TAG system that was able to TAG packets, where each TAG would be configured with a display filter. Then the tagging rules would all be parsed, not first match only.

It would be a different ruleset, so different config file and different input dialog. But very similar to the coloring rules implementation.

If you could implement the emoji functionality like TAGs (where a TAG can be any text, including an emoji. I would very much like this :-)

And I agree with Stig that it would be much nicer to have this implemented as a separate feature instead of an add-on onto the coloring rules engine.

1. so is the thought/vision to have a new menu under View->(emoji/tag rule) . that would then open a dialog box like the coloring rules that has columns
 | checkbox for on/off |  tag/emoji name (for reference purposes) | filter

then a box below to put in the emoji with all the same action buttons that coloring rule has?

2. what would the desired names be since I assume being able to put "text" in there is desirable. Would it be preferred to refer to it as a tag, instead of emoji?

![image](/uploads/54308064ba34c4ab9cb8f380cd3291b4/image.png){width=900 height=492}

That sounds like music to my ears indeed.

And yes, I would vote for them to be called tags and the dialog "View -\> tagging rules". Maybe the columns in the dialog should be:

tag:  the actual tag that will be put in a tags column in the packet list (which could then be a single emoji to implement your original idea)

filter: the display filter that would add the tag to the list of tags

comment: to add some text for reference why this tag was created

One possible usage would be to have a list of tags for different kinds of indicators of compromise and the comment could point to the right name of the IoC or even a link to it's definition.

It would be nice to have the tags into a fields under the "frame" tree, like frame.tag (each tag getting its own field) and then one could create a custom column for that field to show the tags. And one could add a column "count(frame.tag)" to get the amount of tags in each frame too.

Filtering rules to test for the presence of one tag and the absence of another tag are easy to implement that way too, as **frame.tag=="TAG1" and not frame.tag=="TAG2"** would do exactly that.

That's how I envisioned it in my head when I worked on it (I had some code ready, but got sidetracked and never finished it).
thanks for the input. I'll try to get an example together by the end of the week and see what you think.
I'll move this to draft while I work on this.

@SYN-bit @stigbjorlykke  ok this is what I came up with!

Features from the dialog box: 
- Name and comment are displayed in mouseover of tag
- comment is displayed as tooltip when clicked in packet detail view
- scope allows you to add a tag in the current profile, or make it avaliable across all profiles <-let me know what you think of that
- Link allows for the tag to be clicked in the column, and in the packet detail view
- I put a link to emojipedia.org.
-

- column will display all tags that match across the current profile, and "all profile".
- packet details shows all matching tags, and is clickable to url. 1st click highlights the field and shows the comment in tooltip, 2nd click will open the "link"
- ** indicates the tag is across "all profiles"
-
![image](/uploads/ff85aa660907b26e145efbfc83594a4e/image.png){width=460 height=600}

let me know what changes you suggest. Wording, content, anything please. This evolved on me a bit, and I tried to add the things I'd like to have.

Also let me know if I should do a new MR for this, since it's so different from the original. Or should I just change the title and summary of this one.

Here are some observations and suggestions to the tagging system. All in all a great way to help people to observe anomalies  or other things that should stand out.

* I'm not sure I like the scope. I think this will be confusing, it is to me at least and it is not in line with the other things we have like filter buttons, coloring rules etc. The way to have items in multiple profiles for the moment is to use the "Copy from". We could do the same for the tagging rules. For me the scope can be removed.
* If the scope stays, I would like a checkbox when entering the rule, not a popup. The checkbox should be disabled by default in my opinion.
* As already mentioned, but to be complete in my list here too: please move the tag and link entries as columns in the tag list :-)
* You chose a font that is probably good for emoji's, but I like a text tag to be in the same font as the rest of the packet-list. Can there be two different fonts in a cell in the packet-list?
* The size of the tags is now a bit larger than my packet-list font (menlo 13), could the size be made the same as the size of the packet-list font?
* I would like to have a separator between the tags, we normally use a comma, but I can imagine that if you want to go full-emoji, that a space might be better suited (or a pipe character), so maybe a configurable separator would be nice?
* I like the idea of a link, but I don't want to have the tag column clickable (or it should be having an alteration key combination like \<shift\>+\<ctrl\>+click. Another option would be to have an option in the right-click menu to follow the link. Security wise it might be better to just copy the link, as it is done in the http dissector to for the full-uri. Or it should be configurable if you want to open the link or just copy it (with a default to just copy it)

+/* tag_rules.h
+ * Definitions for tagging rules
+ * Copyright 2026, Mark Stout <mark.stout@markstout.com>
+ *

+ * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>

+#pragma once
+#include <glib.h>
+
+#include "ws_symbol_export.h"
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
+
+struct epan_dfilter;
+struct epan_dissect;
+
+#define TAGRULES_FILE_NAME         "tagrules"         /**< Per-profile tagrules file. */
+#define TAGRULES_GLOBAL_FILE_NAME  "tagrules_global"  /**< All-profiles tagrules file (never in a profile subdir). */
+
+/** @file
+ *  Tagging rules — associate user-defined tags with packets via display filters.
+ */
+
+/**
+ * @brief Controls how a tag link is activated in the packet list.
+ */
+typedef enum {
+    TAG_LINK_CLICK_SINGLE = 0, /**< Single left-click opens the link. */
+    TAG_LINK_CLICK_CTRL,       /**< Ctrl+Shift+left-click opens the link. */
+    TAG_LINK_CLICK_NONE        /**< Right-click menu only; click/double-click disabled. */
+} tag_link_click_mode_t;
+
+/**
+ * @brief Global display preferences for the tagging subsystem.
+ *
+ * Applies to all profiles and all rules. Stored in the global (all-profiles)
+ * tagrules file as a header comment: #prefs:sep=XX,size=N,click=N
+ */
+typedef struct _tag_global_prefs {
+    char                  separator;    /**< Between tags when >1 match; '\0' = none. */
+    int                   font_size;    /**< Size as % of row height: 100, 90, 80, 70, 60, 50. 0 = 100%. */
+    tag_link_click_mode_t link_click;   /**< How to activate a tag link. */
+} tag_global_prefs_t;
+
+/**
+ * @brief Data for a single tagging rule.
+ */
+typedef struct _tag_rule {
+    char     *rule_name;              /* Name — also the frame.tag value for filtering */
+    char     *filter_text;            /* Display filter expression */
+    char     *tag_content;            /* Visual content shown in COL_TAG column (emoji / text) */
+    char     *tag_url;                /* Optional URL opened when cell is clicked */
+    char     *comment;                /* Optional reference comment */
+    bool      disabled;
+    bool      global_rule;            /* true = saved in personal config root (all profiles) */
+    struct epan_dfilter *c_tagfilter; /* compiled dfilter, NULL if disabled or invalid */
+} tag_rule_t;
+
+/** @brief A tag rule was added (while importing or cloning).
+ * (tag_rules.c calls this for every rule coming in)
+ *
+ * @param rule  the new tag rule
+ * @param user_data from caller
+ */
+typedef void (*tag_rule_add_cb_func)(tag_rule_t *rule, void *user_data);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Initialize the tag rules subsystem (read from file).
+ *
+ * Loads from the user's personal config file, falling back to the global
+ * data file if no personal file exists.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC void tag_rules_init(void);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Reload the tag rules from disk.
+ *
+ * Frees the current list and re-runs tag_rules_init().
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC void tag_rules_reload(void);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Write tag rules to both the profile and global config files.
+ *
+ * Rules with global_rule=true go to the personal config root (all-profiles file).
+ * Rules with global_rule=false go to the current profile directory.
+ *
+ * @return true if both writes succeeded, false if either failed.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC bool tag_rules_write(void);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Create a new tag rule (g_new0-allocated).
+ *
+ * @param name        Rule name (also used as frame.tag value).
+ * @param filter      Display filter expression.
+ * @param tag_content Visual content for the COL_TAG column.
+ * @param comment     Optional reference comment (may be NULL).
+ * @return Newly allocated tag_rule_t; caller takes ownership.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC tag_rule_t *tag_rule_new(const char *name, const char *filter,
+                                       const char *tag_content,
+                                       const char *tag_url,
+                                       const char *comment);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Delete a single tag rule and free all its memory.

commits_data.title: Qt: Add Tagging Rules subsystem with COL_TAG column
commits_data.message:
Qt: Add Tagging Rules subsystem with COL_TAG column

Introduces a new Tagging Rules feature that lets users associate
visual tags (emoji, text, clickable URLs) with packets via display
filters, independently of coloring rules.

New components:
- epan/tag_rules.c/.h: tag_rule_t struct, file I/O (personal config
  root for "All Profiles" rules, current profile dir for per-profile
  rules), filter compilation, and the tag_rules_* API
- COL_TAG ("%Tg"): new column type rendered by TagColumnDelegate;
  concatenates tag_content of all matching rules per packet
- frame.tag: new FT_STRING proto field populated with the matching
  rule name(s) for display-filter use (frame.tag == "My Rule")
- TaggingRulesDialog (View > Tagging Rules): tree-based editor with
  Name/Filter/Tag Content/Link/Scope/Comment columns, drag-to-reorder,
  import/export, copy-from-profile, and "Copy to Coloring Rule"
- TagColumnDelegate: renders COL_TAG with emoji font; per-segment
  click-to-URL support so each emoji opens its own configured link
- "All Profiles" vs "Current Profile" scope: global rules are stored
  in the personal config root and loaded into every profile; per-profile
  rules live in the profile directory; scope shown in dialog column
- Packet details: frame.tag items are double-clickable to open the
  rule URL; status bar shows the rule comment on click
- Profile switching reloads tag rules alongside color filters
